# Merge Sort in Python

## Implementation

```python
def merge_sort(arr: list) -> list:
    """
    Recursively sorts a list using the merge sort algorithm.
    Time:  O(n log n) in all cases
    Space: O(n) auxiliary
    """
    # Base case: a list of 0 or 1 elements is already sorted
    if len(arr) <= 1:
        return arr

    # --- DIVIDE ---
    # Split the list into two halves at the midpoint
    mid = len(arr) // 2
    left_half  = arr[:mid]
    right_half = arr[mid:]

    # --- CONQUER ---
    # Recursively sort each half
    left_sorted  = merge_sort(left_half)
    right_sorted = merge_sort(right_half)

    # --- MERGE ---
    # Combine the two sorted halves into one sorted list
    return merge(left_sorted, right_sorted)


def merge(left: list, right: list) -> list:
    """
    Merges two sorted lists into a single sorted list.
    This is the heart of merge sort — linear time, O(n).
    """
    result = []       # output list
    i = 0            # index into left
    j = 0            # index into right

    # Compare the front elements of both lists; take the smaller one.
    # The <= (not <) is what guarantees stability (see explanation below).
    while i < len(left) and j < len(right):
        if left[i] <= right[j]:   # <= preserves original order on ties
            result.append(left[i])
            i += 1
        else:
            result.append(right[j])
            j += 1

    # One of the lists is exhausted; append the remaining elements.
    # No further comparison needed — the remainder is already sorted.
